> **Draft.** A first pass written to be rewritten. It runs offline on
> `ic_example_repo()`, so it is checked with the package. Notes in
> *italics* mark where the real version should say more.

A virtual Icechunk array does not hold its data. It holds references:
for each chunk, a file, a byte offset and a length. A table is the
natural form for that information: one row per chunk, with columns for
the chunk's indices and where its bytes are. icechunkr works with
references in that form both ways. It reads any snapshot out as tables
and writes tables back in as commits.

The layout is **byterefs** (version 0.1), from
[raad.virtualize](https://github.com/mdsumner/raad.virtualize). Its tables:

| table | one row per | key columns |
|---|---|---|
| `meta` | key | `key`, `value` |
| `arrays` | array | `array`, `kind`, `storage`, `dims`, `shape`, `chunks`, `dtype`, `fill`, `codec`, `attrs` |
| `sources` | source file | `source`, `size`, `mtime`, `etag` |
| `refs_<array>` | chunk | `dim_0`, `dim_1`, …, `path`, `offset`, `size`, `data` |

*To add: why tables (SQL, Parquet, joins with file catalogues), and how
this relates to kerchunk and VirtualiZarr manifests.*

## Out: a snapshot as tables

```{r}
library(icechunkr)
ex <- ic_example_repo()
repo <- ic_repo_open(ex$path, authorize = ex$authorize)
s <- ic_session_readonly(repo, branch = "main")

br <- ic_to_byterefs(s)
br
br$arrays[, c("array", "kind", "storage", "shape", "chunks", "dtype")]
br$refs("from_bin")[, c("dim_0", "dim_1", "path", "offset", "size")]
```

`from_bin` and `from_nc` are virtual: their rows point into files. The
chunks of `small` were written through a session and are small enough
for Icechunk to keep inline, so their bytes travel in the `data` column.

The same tables can be written to a file, a SQLite database that any SQL
client can open:

```{r}
db <- tempfile(fileext = ".sqlite")
ic_to_byterefs(s, dsn = db)
con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), db)
DBI::dbListTables(con)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT source, mtime FROM sources")
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
```

## In: tables as a repository

`ic_repo_from_byterefs()` goes the other way. It creates a repository,
declares the virtual chunk containers the paths need, writes every
array, and commits once.

```{r}
br2 <- ic_byterefs_read(db)
copy <- ic_repo_from_byterefs(br2, tempfile("copy-"), authorize = ex$authorize,
                              message = "rebuilt from byterefs")
s2 <- ic_session_readonly(copy, branch = "main")
identical(ic_get(s2, "from_bin/c/2/0"), ic_get(s, "from_bin/c/2/0"))
cmp <- ic_byterefs_compare(br, ic_to_byterefs(s2))
all(cmp$ok)
br2$close()   # a byterefs store read from SQLite holds the connection open
```

When the `sources` table has a modification time (or an ETag, for
objects in a bucket), it is recorded as a checksum on that source's
references. If the source file changes after the references were made,
Icechunk refuses to read its chunks rather than return the wrong bytes.
The example repository was made without checksums, so its `mtime` column
is empty.

## Writing through DBI

The DBI connection is a way to read, and also a way to write. Appending
rows to `arrays` creates arrays, and appending rows to `refs_<array>`
sets chunk references. A transaction becomes one Icechunk commit.

Start an empty repository that may read from the example's source
directory:

```{r}
library(DBI)
path <- tempfile("built-")
con <- dbConnect(Icechunk(), path, create = TRUE,
                 containers = ic_container(ex$authorize, "local", path = ex$source),
                 authorize = ex$authorize)
dbListTables(con)
```

Describe an array, then its chunks. `grid.bin` holds 64 x 48
little-endian float32 values. Here they become an array of 16-row
chunks:

```{r}
dbBegin(con)
dbAppendTable(con, "arrays", data.frame(
  array = "grid", kind = "data", storage = "referenced",
  dims = '["y","x"]', shape = "[64,48]", chunks = "[16,48]", dtype = "<f4",
  fill = "NaN", attrs = '{"units":"none"}'))
dbAppendTable(con, "refs_grid", data.frame(
  dim_0 = 0:3, dim_1 = 0L,
  path = file.path(ex$source, "grid.bin"), offset = (0:3) * 3072, size = 3072))
dbCommit(con, "grid: four blocks of grid.bin")
dbGetQuery(con, 'SELECT dim_0, "offset", size FROM refs_grid')
```

The bytes come from the source file, through Icechunk:

```{r}
rs <- ic_session_readonly(ic_repo_open(path, authorize = ex$authorize), branch = "main")
x <- readBin(ic_get(rs, "grid/c/3/0"), "double", 768, size = 4, endian = "little")
all.equal(x, ex$values[2304 + 1:768])
```

Rows added later for a source already in the repository take that
source's checksum, if it has one, from the `sources` table. Without
`dbBegin()`, each append commits on its own:

```{r}
dbAppendTable(con, "refs_grid", data.frame(
  dim_0 = 3L, dim_1 = 0L, path = file.path(ex$source, "grid.bin"), offset = 0, size = 3072))
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT message FROM ancestry")
```

`dbRollback()` discards an open transaction. If someone else committed to
the branch in the meantime, `dbCommit(rebase = TRUE)` replays your changes
on top of theirs, with Icechunk's conflict detection deciding what can
merge.

```{r}
other <- ic_session_writable(ic_repo_open(path, authorize = ex$authorize), "main")
ic_set(other, "zarr.json", charToRaw('{"zarr_format":3,"node_type":"group","attributes":{"by":"someone else"}}'))
ic_commit(other, "a concurrent edit")

dbBegin(con)
dbAppendTable(con, "refs_grid", data.frame(
  dim_0 = 2L, dim_1 = 0L, path = file.path(ex$source, "grid.bin"), offset = 6144, size = 3072))
dbCommit(con, "restore block 2", rebase = TRUE)
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT message FROM ancestry")
dbDisconnect(con)
```
